clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (41 FR 37301), as amended by EO 12107 section 2-101 (the Office of Personnel Management substituted for the Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404). The order states no end, and no held later order revokes or supersedes it. The three bounded machine searches (current-law:usc, U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; current-law:ecfr, eCFR as of 2026-10-14; later-events:ofr_catalog, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) were read for coverage and show no revocation or supersession. The Federal Register document 2026-13154 (91 FR 39361, an OPM final rule published June 30, 2026) still applies the rule as an existing requirement: it states that an individual cannot be admitted to competitive examination or given an appointment in the competitive service unless he or she is a citizen or national of the United States and cites Executive Order 11935 for that rule. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The sole paragraph amends Civil Service Rule VII by adding section 7.4 (Citizenship): no person is admitted to competitive examination, and no person is given an appointment in the competitive service, unless a citizen or national of the United States; the Commission may, to the extent permitted by law, authorize the appointment of aliens when necessary to promote the efficiency of the service in specific cases or for temporary appointments. The order carries no sunset, condition or duration. EO 12107 section 2-101 lists EO 11935 under subsection (a) and amends the listed orders by substituting Office of Personnel Management wording for Civil Service Commission wording, effective January 1, 1979; that amendment changes the agency named in paragraph (c) and leaves the rule in force. The held eCFR text of 5 CFR 7.3 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-7.3.txt, not a packet evidence record) reproduces paragraphs (a) to (c) with OPM in place of the Commission under a source note reading E.O. 11935, 41 FR 37301, Sept. 3, 1976, redesignated by E.O. 13197, 66 FR 7853, Jan. 25, 2001. The held text of EO 13197 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_13197.txt, also not a packet evidence record, so it is not attached as a later event) strikes Civil Service Rule VII section 7.2 and redesignates sections 7.3 and 7.4 as 7.2 and 7.3, and its table of sections lists 7.3 Citizenship; it renumbers the section and keeps the rule, so it does not end the clause. EO 13940 (2020), section 2(c) as held, directs agency heads to review compliance with EO 11935; it recites the order and neither amends nor ends it.

research_rationale:
EO 11935 (41 FR 37301, signed September 2, 1976) amends Civil Service Rule VII (5 CFR Part 7) by adding a new section 7.4, Citizenship: only citizens or nationals of the United States may be admitted to competitive examination or appointed in the competitive service, with an exception the Commission may authorize by law for aliens in specific cases or temporary appointments. I read the complete held Federal Register original; the order is one paragraph with one added section and no sunset or condition, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. Held later instruments: EO 12107 (signed December 28, 1978; effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the orders listed in its section 2-101, which includes EO 11935; it is attached as a later event. EO 13940 (2020) recites EO 11935 in a compliance-review direction and does not amend it. A June 30, 2026 OPM final rule (FR Doc. 2026-13154) restates the rule as existing law. The held 5 CFR 7.3 source note records the redesignation by EO 13197 (January 25, 2001); the held text of EO 13197 renumbers section 7.4 as 7.3 and lists 7.3 Citizenship in its table of sections, so it keeps the rule. That text is held in the repository but is not a packet evidence record, so the claim describes it and does not cite it as a later event. A search of the held texts for the number 11935 finds only EO 12107's list, EO 13940, Federal Register pages that cite or apply the order, and CFR texts that apply it; none revokes or supersedes it. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions) record no revocation or supersession. The clause continues on the original text as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
